text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
GENERAL
ALL PAPERS
-- U.S. Senate Majority leader Trent Lott said it is a fait accompli that NATO will invite Hungary to accession negotiations at the Madrid summit next week.
-- Postabank and the state privatisation agency APV are to carrty out a 17 billion forint worth asset swap under a cabinet resultion agreed on Thursday.

-- Opposition party Democratic Forum (MDF) condemned what it called a coalition attempt to shut down a commission dealing with a privatisation scandal over irregular payments to an adviser, Marta Tocsik.
VILAGGAZDASAG

-- A State Audit Office report blames former Finance Minister and former Budapest bank chief Lajos Bokros for shortcomings in the bank's privatisation, claiming that he hid the real terms of the contract from the government.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
-- Opposition Smallholders' Party president Jozsef Torgyan called on Interior Miniter Gabor Kuncze to resign as he was responsible for a privatisation scandal, the so-called Tocsik case.
KOSSUTH RADIO
-- Prime Minister Gyula Horn denied that the government wanted to cover up the Tocsik case.
NEPSZABADSAG
-- Police are seeking the extradition of a Ukrainian citizen in connection with a May 5 incident in which a Range Rover was blown up in the town Szentendre.
BUSINESS
ALL PAPERS

-- The Fair Competition Officwe fined OTP Bank five million forints for illegally charging commission on foreign currency withdrawals from individual foreign currency accounts and imposing an embargo fee for dormant accounts.
-- The financial services group Bankar has purchased the stock mexchange membership of the brokerage Gog Ertekpair Rt as part of a merger deal.
-- Magyar Cukor Rt has decided to close down its Ercsi sugar factory this year and sugar producers said that it may close the Sarakd and Mezohegyes plants also.
NAPI GAZDASAG
-- The growth in industrial production and producer prices slowed down in May, according to preliminary calculations by the Central Statistical Office.
-- Blackburn International, controlled by Fotex Chairman and CEO Gabor Varszegi, purchased 50,000 Fotex shares on June 30 and 24,563 shares on July 1.
VILAGGAZDASAG

-- Interest rates on forint loans of less than 12 months granted to entrepreneurs dropped to an average of 22 percent by May, while deposits paid an average of 17.9 percent, the National Bank of Hungary said.
-- Hungary's second national telecommunications service provider was founded under the name of MKMTEL Tavkozlesi Kommunikacios Kft.
-- The Moscow-based Russisky Credit Bank and Dresdner Bank signed a $43 million loan gareement for the supply of 403 Ikarus buses to Moscow.
NEPSZABADSAG

-- Agricultural ministry analysts put this year's wheat crop at 5.1 million tonnes, or 4.1 tonnes per hectare on average, procurement prices at 18,000 t0 24,000 forints per tonne and exports at between two and 2.5 million tonnes.
-- Budapest-Vienna train journeys can now be completed in two hours following the completion of a track upgrade between Budapest and the Hegyeshalom border station.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
-- Hungarian companies hope to participate in the construction of the new Kazakh capital Akmola, located 1,400 kilometres from the current capital Almaty.
-- National air carrier Malev carried its one millionth passenger this year on Thursday, two weeks earlier than last year, Malev said.
